analysis.subject: history
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers Apollo 11 objectives, crew and spacecraft, launch on July 16 1969, translunar travel, lunar orbit insertion, descent and landing in Sea of Tranquility, surface experiments and samples, ascent and docking, return flight and splashdown on July 24 1969, plus earlier test milestones.

overview.headline: First crewed lunar landing and return flight from launch to splashdown

keyPoints.point: Students learn the primary goal was a crewed lunar landing and safe return to Earth.
keyPoints.quote: perform a crewed lunar landing and return to Earth.

keyPoints.point: Students learn the crew launched from Cape Kennedy on July 16, 1969 carrying Commander Neil Armstrong aboard.
keyPoints.quote: Apollo 11 launched from Cape Kennedy on July 16, 1969, carrying Commander Neil Armstrong

keyPoints.point: Students learn astronauts completed deployment of solar wind composition experiment and seismic experiment package on the surface.
keyPoints.quote: deployment of a solar wind composition experiment, seismic experiment package and a Laser Ranging Retroreflector.

keyPoints.point: Students learn the Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility at the documented latitude on July 20, 1969.
keyPoints.quote: the Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility in Site 2 at 0 degrees, 41 minutes, 15 seconds north latitude

keyPoints.point: Students learn the capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean near the recovery ship after the return flight.
keyPoints.quote: Apollo 11 splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, 13 miles from the recovery ship USS Hornet.

keyTerms.gloss: trajectory that allows return to Earth without engine firing if needed
keyTerms.quote: This was to be the last Apollo mission to fly a “free-return” trajectory

keyTerms.gloss: planned engine burns to adjust course during flight between Earth and moon
keyTerms.quote: the second of four scheduled midcourse corrections programmed for the flight.

keyTerms.gloss: path of the spacecraft circling the moon before descent
lunar plain where the Eagle landed and astronauts walked
keyTerms.quote: the Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility in Site 2 at 0 degrees, 41 minutes, 15 seconds north latitude

keyTerms.gloss: orbit that carries the spacecraft from Earth toward the moon
keyTerms.quote: placing Apollo 11 into a translunar orbit.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Mission is told as a dated sequence and students benefit from ordering launch, landing and splashdown events chronologically.
componentPlan.focusQuote: Apollo 11 launched from Cape Kennedy on July 16, 1969, carrying Commander Neil Armstrong

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Key facts about objectives, crew, experiments and landing site are directly checkable from short quoted sentences.
componentPlan.focusQuote: deployment of a solar wind composition experiment, seismic experiment package and a Laser Ranging Retroreflector.
